items.title: Library supplement: Radial differential divergence

source.attribution: Generic exposition of classical sphere calculus; no primary-textbook completion or novelty claim.

items.statement: Write \(E_n=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S_n=\{x\in E_n:\|x\|=1\}\), and \(M_{n,N}=S_n^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). The dimensions are natural numbers and may be zero. For every natural \(n\), every map \(W:S_n\to E_n\), and every \(x\in S_n\), sum the total scalar derivatives at zero of the coordinate lines \(t\mapsto(W^{\mathrm r}(x+t e_j))_j\), where \(e_j\) is the standard Euclidean coordinate vector. Each total scalar derivative is the ordinary derivative if it exists and zero otherwise. This definition makes no C¹ or tangency assertion. Under intrinsic C¹ regularity the sum equals the ambient Fréchet trace; its ordinary intrinsic vector-field divergence interpretation additionally requires \(W(x)\perp x\) at every sphere point. For a nontangent map it is not asserted to be the divergence of its tangent projection. Here \(W^{\mathrm r}(z)=W(\|z\|^{-1}z)\) for \(z\ne0\) and \(W^{\mathrm r}(0)=0\). Intrinsic C¹ refers to the ordinary stereographic smooth structure on \(S_n\).
assumptions: Use the indicated canonical real Euclidean, unit-sphere and finite-product carriers; no positive-dimension restriction is imposed.
This is a definition or abbreviation. It imposes no unstated regularity, tangency, integrability or probability hypothesis.
